title: [Activity] Review the Results of our Algorithm Evaluation.

cues.en: Okay, so you can see the final results here and they do seem to make sense.
cues.zh: 好，這裡可以看到最後結果，看來確實合理。

cues.en: Let's expand that a bit.
cues.zh: 把它放大一點。

cues.en: Remember we're comparing SVD, or singular value decomposition, against random recommendations here.
cues.zh: 記得，這裡比較的是 SVD，也就是奇異值分解，與隨機推薦。

cues.en: And SVD is one of the best algorithms available right now, so it shouldn't be a surprise that SVD beats random recommendations in accuracy and hit rate no matter how we measure it.
cues.zh: SVD 是目前最好的演算法之一，因此不管用什麼方式衡量，SVD 在準確程度與命中率都勝過隨機推薦，並不意外。

cues.en: Remember, lower RMSE and MAE scores are better, as they are measuring errors.
cues.zh: 記得，RMSE 與 MAE 是衡量誤差，所以越低越好。

cues.en: This can be a little confusing since we talk about these metrics in terms of accuracy and you would think that more accuracy is better, but the actual numbers for root mean squared error
cues.zh: 這可能有點令人混淆，因為我們用準確程度來談這些指標，而你會覺得準確程度越高越好；但均方根誤差

cues.en: or mean absolute error are measuring error, the opposite of accuracy.
cues.zh: 與平均絕對誤差的實際數值，是衡量與準確程度相反的誤差。

cues.en: So it's good that SVD has lower RMSE and MAE than the random recommender.
cues.zh: 因此，SVD 的 RMSE 與 MAE 比隨機推薦低，是好事。

cues.en: Higher hit rates, however, are better, and no matter how we measure it, hit rate, cumulative hit rate, or average reciprocal hit rate, SVD does a better job.
cues.zh: 不過，命中率越高越好；不管是命中率、累積命中率或平均倒數命中率，SVD 表現都比較好。

cues.en: The actual numbers here are still quite small, however, and that's to be expected.
cues.zh: 然而，這裡的實際數字仍然很小，這是預期中的。

cues.en: It's really hard to get a hit with leave-one-out cross validation, especially when you have a lot of items to choose from.
cues.zh: 留一交叉驗證很難命中，尤其有很多項目可以選時。

cues.en: Now we get into coverage, diversity and novelty, and these metrics are ones you need to apply some common sense to, as it's not a clear higher-is-better sort of thing.
cues.zh: 接著看覆蓋率、多樣性與新穎性，這些指標必須運用常識判斷，因為不是明確地越高越好。

cues.en: There are trade offs involved with these metrics, remember.
cues.zh: 記得，這些指標涉及取捨。

cues.en: Coverage, for example, is a bit lower, but that's just because we're enforcing a quality threshold on the top-N recommendations we're making with SVD, while our random recommender isn't actually
cues.zh: 例如，覆蓋率比較低，只是因為對 SVD 的 Top-N 推薦設定了品質門檻；而隨機推薦系統實際上並不是

cues.en: making totally random recommendations, it's predicting movie ratings using what's called a normal distribution centered around the average rating value, which ends up meaning all of the rating predictions it makes
cues.zh: 完全隨機推薦，而是用以平均評分為中心的常態分布預測電影評分，結果所有評分預測

cues.en: fall above our rating threshold, giving us 100% coverage.
cues.zh: 都高於我們的評分門檻，因此覆蓋率是 100%。

cues.en: Having 100% coverage at the expense of having bad recommendations isn't a trade off worth making.
cues.zh: 為了 100% 覆蓋率，犧牲成很差的推薦，並不值得。

cues.en: Diversity is also lower with SVD, but you can see this as a good and expected thing.
cues.zh: SVD 的多樣性也較低，但這可以視為預期中的好事。

cues.en: Since people tend to have somewhat consistent interests, you'd think that good recommendations for a specific user would be more similar to each other than ones pulled at random that are not personalized in any way.
cues.zh: 由於人們的興趣通常有一定一致性，你會預期，對特定使用者的好推薦，應該比完全沒有個人化的隨機推薦更彼此相似。

cues.en: Finally, novelty is lower with SVD, but again, that's good and expected.
cues.zh: 最後，SVD 的新穎性較低，但同樣是預期中的好事。

cues.en: You would expect that just picking random movies to recommend would give you a high novelty score since it's pulling all sorts of movies out of the long tail, while SVD would end up discovering that
cues.zh: 你會預期，隨機挑電影推薦，會從長尾中抽出各式各樣的電影，產生很高的新穎性分數；而 SVD 則會發現，

cues.en: good movie recommendations tend to be more popular movies.
cues.zh: 好的電影推薦通常是較熱門的電影。

cues.en: Popular movies are popular for a reason.
cues.zh: 熱門電影之所以熱門，有其原因。

cues.en: They appeal to a lot of people and are good recommendations for a lot of people if they haven't seen them yet.
cues.zh: 它們吸引很多人，如果那些人還沒看過，就是很適合推薦的電影。

cues.en: So again, a lower novelty score here isn't a bad thing, it's just a measure of the nature of the recommendations you're making and how obscure they are.
cues.zh: 因此，再次強調，這裡新穎性比較低，不是壞事，它只是衡量推薦的性質，以及有多冷門。

cues.en: But anyway, it works!
cues.zh: 總之，它能運作。

cues.en: We have a framework now that will let us test and evaluate new recommendation algorithms as we go through them and it makes it really easy to do so.
cues.zh: 現在有一個框架，讓我們在接下來介紹新推薦演算法時，能輕鬆測試與評估。

cues.en: A framework like this is something you can also use in the real world, as you'll often want to prototype new ideas without necessarily evaluating them online right away, and it's also useful for combining recommendations
cues.zh: 這類框架也能用於真實世界，因為你經常會想先替新想法做原型，不一定立刻在線上評估；它也適合將多種演算法的

cues.en: from multiple recommendation algorithms together, which can sometimes be a very powerful technique.
cues.zh: 推薦組合起來，有時這是非常強大的技術。

cues.en: With all of this out of the way, we can finally start experimenting with different algorithms and go into more depth about how they work.
cues.zh: 處理完這些之後，終於可以開始實驗不同演算法，更深入了解它們如何運作。
